treasuryClosingCash20201231.limits: A shared national Treasury Federal Reserve Account closing balance, not a Social Security/local appropriation. All DTS figures are rounded to the nearest million. Under REVIEW15 this remains research evidence only; no Treasury stock enters the candidate.

treasuryClosingCash20201231.openingBoundary: Closing business-day balance before the 2021-01-01 opening; publication after reporting close is not actor knowledge at opening.
treasuryClosingCash20201231.independentConfirmation: Federal Reserve 2020 Annual Report statistical tables, Treasury general account, December 31, 2020: 1,728,569 million USD.

oasiNetBenefitPayments2020.limits: Calendar-2020 OASI net benefit payments. Includes retirement and survivors; scheduled-benefit-year adjustment excludes January 3, 2021 benefits paid December 31, 2020 from the 2020 cost figure. Retrospective annual flow, never cash, allocation, cap or cutoff.

oasiNetPayrollTaxContributions2020.limits: Annual net payroll tax contributions: a continuing receipt mechanism, not prepaid 2021 liquid stock or individual tax receipts.

oasiBenefitTaxReceipts2020.limits: Annual income from taxation of benefits; not a liquid stock or each due payment source.

oasiInvestmentIncome2020.limits: Total investment income and interest adjustments; separate from net payroll/benefit tax receipts and not new net income to consolidated Treasury.

oasiInvestedAssets20201231.limits: Entirely special-issue Treasury securities in the OASI portfolio, not cash. No securities are converted to model cash.

oasiUndisbursedBalances20201231.limits: Table III.A1 footnote g: primarily January 3, 2021 benefits already paid December 31, 2020, plus relatively small Treasury credit pending securities redemption. Not an available $18.570B cash opening.

oasiTotalAssetReserves20201231.limits: Adjusted scheduled-benefit-year assets combine securities and undisbursed amounts. Do not initialize liquid cash from this total.

retiredWorkerMeanPayableJanuary2021.limits: SSA labels this estimated average payable after the 1.3% COLA. It is not an actual individual award, the realized January mean, a benefit formula, an eligibility measure or an observed disposable/net cash amount. Individual career-length scaling and variation remain uncalibrated.
retiredWorkerMeanPayableJanuary2021.releaseDateBasis: The October 13, 2020 SSA announcement links the 2021 fact sheet; the current migrated factsheet itself has no separate original publication timestamp.

ssaPaymentDayRule2020.limits: 20 CFR 404.1807 uses the insured worker birth day: 1–10 second Wednesday, 11–20 third Wednesday, later fourth Wednesday; actual exceptions include pre-May-1997 entitlement, SSI/deemed income, foreign residence, state Medicare-premium arrangements and continuous entitlement. Weekend/federal-holiday payments arrive the preceding business day. Source rule dates do not establish which saved fictional claimant belongs in which cycle.

january2021CalendarExamples.dateStatus: Wednesday examples are deterministic calendar derivations from the sourced rule, not retrieved individual payment rows; early cycle1 date is confirmed in SSA 2021 Trustees footnotes.

ssaPaymentDayRule2020.candidateCalendarStatus: NOT_IMPLEMENTED: existing fixed-day/first-due calendar remains expressly ESTIMATED. No scheduler rewrite in this packet.

treasuryGrossDebtCashIssues20201231.limits: One actual cash-day category, rounded in millions. Gross debt issues are borrowed receipts rather than earned income; debt redemptions are outflows; this Social Security EFT line is not a retired-worker-only amount or individual beneficiary crosswalk. No chronology of fungible dollars is inferred.

treasuryTrustFundCashBoundary.limits: Treasury distinguishes trust-fund balances from cash and describes access to ongoing tax revenues and federal debt issuance. Its financial-report cash-and-other-monetary-assets figure also includes assets other than the operating TGA balance; it must not replace a program-specific cash stock.

trustFundRedemptionFinancing.limits: Trust-fund bond redemption, interest and general-revenue transfers provide no new net income to Treasury. In a unified-budget deficit they are financed through taxes, spending changes or additional borrowing. They are not automatic newly generated capital for a local payer.
